Component

message scroller

Install

A chat transcript scroller: follows a streaming reply at the live edge, anchors new turns, opens saved threads without a flash, keeps your place when history loads, and offers a jump-to-latest button.

Can you walk me through how a streaming chat should scroll?
Sure. The short version: move the reader only when they asked to move.
What does that mean while a reply is arriving?
If you are at the live edge the new text stays in view. If you scroll away, it leaves you alone.
And when I send a new message?
Your message lands near the top with a peek of the previous turn, and the reply grows into the room below it.
Then what happens once the reply fills the screen?
Following takes over from the anchor, so the newest words stay visible until you scroll up.
How do I get back after scrolling up?
A jump button appears at the bottom. It is a real button, so the keyboard reaches it too.
Does it work for a saved conversation?
Yes: it opens at the end (or at your last message) without flashing the top first.
Scrollable: none

shadcn-dioxus add message_scroller

Also adds the components and crates this one needs. First time in this app? Set up the CLI and your app first.

Copy the component source and CSS into your app. Import the shared theme CSS once near your app root.

use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonSize, ButtonVariant};
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use dioxus_icons::lucide::ArrowDown;
use dioxus_primitives::dioxus_attributes::attributes;
use dioxus_primitives::merge_attributes;
use dioxus_primitives::message_scroller::{
    self, MessageScrollerContentProps, MessageScrollerItemProps, MessageScrollerProps,
    MessageScrollerProviderProps, MessageScrollerRowsProps, MessageScrollerViewportProps,
};

// Re-exported so a demo (or a consumer's own page) can write
// `use crate::components::message_scroller::*;` and reach the commands hook,
// the scrollability signal and the option enums without a second import from
// `dioxus_primitives` -- the same convention `carousel`'s wrapper follows.
#[allow(unused_imports)] // a consumer-facing surface; this crate's own demos use a subset
pub use dioxus_primitives::message_scroller::{
    use_message_scroller, use_message_scroller_scrollable, use_message_scroller_visibility,
    DefaultScrollPosition, MessageScrollerApi, MessageScrollerDirection, ScrollAlign,
    ScrollBehavior, ScrollFade, ScrollToMessageOptions, Scrollable, Virtualization, Visibility,
};

/// The headless root: owns the scroll controller and renders no element.
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerProvider(props: MessageScrollerProviderProps) -> Element {
    rsx! {
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerProvider {
            auto_scroll: props.auto_scroll,
            default_scroll_position: props.default_scroll_position,
            scroll_edge_threshold: props.scroll_edge_threshold,
            scroll_previous_item_peek: props.scroll_previous_item_peek,
            scroll_margin: props.scroll_margin,
            virtualize: props.virtualize,
            {props.children}
        }
    }
}

/// The frame: fills its parent (place it in a height-constrained container).
#[component]
pub fn MessageScroller(props: MessageScrollerProps) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div {
        class: "dx-message-scroller",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, props.attributes]);

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScroller { attributes: merged, {props.children} }
    }
}

/// The scrollable element. Its edge fade is the `fade` prop (default
/// [`ScrollFade::Bottom`], `dx-scroll-fade-b` from `dx-effects.css`; without that file the fade
/// is simply absent).
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerViewport(props: MessageScrollerViewportProps) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div {
        class: "dx-message-scroller-viewport",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller-viewport",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, props.attributes]);

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerViewport {
            preserve_scroll_on_prepend: props.preserve_scroll_on_prepend,
            fade: props.fade,
            attributes: merged,
            {props.children}
        }
    }
}

/// The transcript column holding the rows.
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerContent(props: MessageScrollerContentProps) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div {
        class: "dx-message-scroller-content",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller-content",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, props.attributes]);

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerContent {
            spacer_class: props.spacer_class,
            attributes: merged,
            {props.children}
        }
    }
}

/// One transcript row: a message, marker, typing indicator or separator.
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerItem(props: MessageScrollerItemProps) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div {
        class: "dx-message-scroller-item",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller-item",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, props.attributes]);

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerItem {
            message_id: props.message_id,
            scroll_anchor: props.scroll_anchor,
            attributes: merged,
            {props.children}
        }
    }
}

/// A long transcript's rows, grouped in chunks of 20 that the browser skips as a unit
/// (one skippable element per row costs main-thread time per scroll frame in proportion to the
/// row count). Use it in place of a `for` loop of `MessageScrollerItem`s.
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerRows(props: MessageScrollerRowsProps) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div {
        class: "dx-message-scroller-chunk",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller-chunk",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, props.attributes]);

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerRows {
            count: props.count,
            start: props.start,
            render_row: props.render_row,
            attributes: merged,
        }
    }
}

/// The jump control: scrolls to the end (or start) of the transcript. Renders
/// the themed `Button` (a secondary icon button by default) with an arrow and a
/// screen-reader label unless `children` are given.
#[component]
pub fn MessageScrollerButton(
    #[props(default)] direction: MessageScrollerDirection,
    #[props(default = ScrollBehavior::Smooth)] behavior: ScrollBehavior,
    #[props(default = ButtonVariant::Secondary)] variant: ButtonVariant,
    #[props(default = ButtonSize::IconSm)] size: ButtonSize,
    #[props(default)] onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = button)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Option<Element>,
) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(button {
        class: "dx-message-scroller-button",
        "data-slot": "message-scroller-button",
    });
    let merged = merge_attributes(vec![base, attributes]);
    let label = match direction {
        MessageScrollerDirection::End => "Scroll to end",
        MessageScrollerDirection::Start => "Scroll to start",
    };

    rsx! {
        document::Link { rel: "stylesheet", href: asset!("/src/components/message_scroller/style.css") }
        message_scroller::MessageScrollerButton {
            direction,
            behavior,
            onclick,
            attributes: merged,
            r#as: move |attributes: Vec<Attribute>| {
                rsx! {
                    Button { variant, size, attributes,
                        if let Some(children) = children.clone() {
                            {children}
                        } else {
                            ArrowDown { size: "16px", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                            span { class: "dx-message-scroller-sr-only", "{label}" }
                        }
                    }
                }
            },
            {}
        }
    }
}

The message scroller is the scroll container for a chat transcript. It owns scroll and nothing else: where the thread opens, whether it follows a reply that is still arriving, where a new turn lands, keeping your place while older messages load above you, and a button to get back to the latest message. It does not own messages, models, transport or persistence; the rows are whatever you put inside a MessageScrollerItem (here, Message, Bubble and Marker).

It is a port of shadcn/ui's message-scroller. The one rule behind every behavior: never move the reader against their intent.

MessageScrollerProvider { auto_scroll: true,
    MessageScroller {
        MessageScrollerViewport {
            MessageScrollerContent {
                for message in messages() {
                    MessageScrollerItem {
                        key: "{message.id}",
                        message_id: "{message.id}",
                        scroll_anchor: message.is_user,
                        Message { /* ... */ }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        MessageScrollerButton {}
    }
}

MessageScroller fills its parent, so place it in a container with a fixed or constrained height.

  • MessageScrollerProvider is the headless root. It owns the scroll controller and the behavior props, and renders no element.
  • MessageScroller is the frame. It lays out the viewport and the jump button.
  • MessageScrollerViewport is the scrolling element. It is role="region" with aria-label="Messages" and tabindex="0", so keyboard users can scroll it.
  • MessageScrollerContent holds the rows. It is role="log" with aria-relevant="additions": a new row is announced, token-by-token text growth inside a row is not.
  • MessageScrollerItem wraps every direct child of the content. A row can be a message, a marker, a typing indicator, a separator, or a "load earlier" row.
  • MessageScrollerButton scrolls to the end (or, with direction: MessageScrollerDirection::Start, the start).

With auto_scroll, the transcript follows new content while the reader is at the live edge. Scrolling away releases it, whether by the wheel, touch, the scroll keys (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End, Space) or by dragging the scrollbar, and so does an explicit jump to a message. New chunks then arrive without moving the reader. The jump button, or scroll_to_end, re-engages following.

Following is off by default: nothing moves unless you ask it to.

Mark the row that starts a turn with scroll_anchor (usually the user's message). When a new anchor is appended, the viewport scrolls it near the top, keeping scroll_previous_item_peek pixels of the previous row visible above it, and the reply streams into the room below. Once the reply fills the viewport the reader is back at the live edge and auto_scroll takes over. Anchoring is not tied to a role: any row can be an anchor.

default_scroll_position picks where the transcript opens on its first non-empty render: End (the default), Start, or LastAnchor: the user's latest message with its reply below it, falling back to the end when that turn already fits.

The prop is live. Change it on a mounted provider (it is a ReadSignal, so a signal or a plain value both work) and the transcript applies the new opening position to the thread that is already on screen, with no remount; the opening_position example does exactly that from its tabs. Only the first paint is guarded (below): a later change never hides the viewport again.

Avoiding a flash on load

A scroll container always opens at the top, so a server-rendered transcript would show its oldest messages and then jump. When the position is End or LastAnchor, the root and viewport render data-pending-scroll (identically on the server and on the hydrating client) and the styled viewport stays hidden until the position is applied. The attribute is removed for an empty transcript too, and a few seconds after load as a failsafe, so a transcript can never stay hidden. The guard covers the first paint only and never hides the viewport again, not even when default_scroll_position later changes.

Older messages prepended above the current ones do not move what you are reading: the viewport keeps the first visible row where it is (preserve_scroll_on_prepend, on by default). Give rows a stable message_id, so the scroller has a specific row to hold.

A long thread should not lay out and paint thousands of rows that nobody can see. virtualize on the provider picks how the scroller keeps off-screen rows cheap:

MessageScrollerProvider { virtualize: Virtualization::ContentVisibility, /* ... */ }
  • Virtualization::None: every row is fully rendered all the time. Use it for short threads, or when a row's content cannot tolerate being skipped.
  • Virtualization::ContentVisibility (the default): rows stay in the DOM and the browser skips layout and paint for the ones that are off-screen (content-visibility: auto, with contain-intrinsic-size: auto so it remembers each row's last rendered height). Because the rows are real DOM, the accessibility tree and text selection keep reaching every message, including the ones scrolled far out of view, and so does the browser's find-in-page where the engine supports it (see below). The scroller never skips three groups of rows: the rows at the live edge (so the end geometry is exact while a reply streams), the row that holds focus, and the rows that hold the ends of the current selection. It marks them with data-keep-rendered, which the stylesheet excludes from skipping. Tune the first-render height guess with the --dx-message-scroller-row-estimate custom property (default 10rem; a chunk's guess is its rows' guesses plus the gaps between them).

Long threads: render the rows through MessageScrollerRows. The browser does per-frame work for every element it may skip, so skipping each row separately costs main-thread time proportional to the row count on every scroll frame: 20.3 ms per frame for the 2,000-row example below (release build, headless Chromium, 4-core VM), against a 16.7 ms frame budget. MessageScrollerRows groups the rows in chunks of 20 and the browser skips each chunk as one element, which brought the same scroll to 3.7 ms per frame (measured on a heavily loaded machine, which includes the scroller's own controller work; the spec asserts under 8 ms on a release build). Use it in place of a for loop of MessageScrollerItems; the scroller treats the chunks as transparent, so following the stream, anchoring, prepend preservation and jumping to a message work as before, and the chunk holding the live edge, focus or an end of the selection is the one that stays rendered:

MessageScrollerContent {
    MessageScrollerRows {
        count: messages.len(),
        render_row: move |i: usize| rsx! {
            MessageScrollerItem { key: "{messages[i].id}", message_id: "{messages[i].id}",
                /* the row */
            }
        },
    }
}

Chunks are grouped by absolute position, so when you prepend older messages, lower start by the number prepended (MessageScrollerRows { start: -(prepended as isize), .. }, accumulating) and every existing row stays in its chunk and keeps its DOM node. Rows written directly as children of the content still work and keep the per-row behaviour: fine for a few hundred rows.

Find-in-page support. Skipped content stays findable in Chromium and in Firefox 125 and later, and in Safari from Safari 26. In Safari 18 through 25 the browser's find-in-page does not find text inside a skipped (off-screen) row (WebKit bug 283846): there the text is still in the DOM, the accessibility tree and any selection, but Cmd+F will not match it until the row has been scrolled into view. If your users depend on find-in-page across a long thread on those versions, use Virtualization::None, or give them a search of your own built on scroll_to_message.

Mounting only a window of rows is a possible future option, but it is not part of this API and not planned for now: unmounted rows are not in the DOM, so native find-in-page, screen-reader history and a selection that spans messages could not reach them, and an app would have to provide its own search. ContentVisibility keeps the DOM, the accessibility tree and selection whole (and find-in-page where supported, as above), and is the right size for hundreds to low thousands of turns.

The long example below keeps 2,000 rows in the DOM, rendered through MessageScrollerRows: only the chunks in view are laid out, and following a reply still lands exactly at the end. In browsers that support it, find-in-page still locates text in a row far off-screen.

use_message_scroller() returns commands you can call from any descendant of the provider:

let scroller = use_message_scroller();
scroller.scroll_to_end(ScrollBehavior::Smooth);
scroller.scroll_to_start(ScrollBehavior::Auto);
scroller.scroll_to_message("m42", ScrollToMessageOptions::default());
scroller.scroll_to_message(
    "m42",
    ScrollToMessageOptions {
        align: ScrollAlign::Center,
        behavior: ScrollBehavior::Instant,
        scroll_margin: Some(24.0),
    },
);

ScrollBehavior is Auto (jump, or follow the viewport's CSS scroll-behavior), Instant (jump now whatever that CSS says) or Smooth (animated; Smooth becomes Auto under prefers-reduced-motion). scroll_margin is the margin on the aligned edge for that one call; None uses the provider's scroll_margin. align is Start, Center, End or Nearest.

The commands are fire-and-forget and return nothing. They travel to the scroll controller over a one-way channel and run there on a later turn of the event loop, so a bool ("did that row exist?") could only be a guess made before the answer exists. A return value that can lie is worse than none, so there is none. Observe the outcome instead: use_message_scroller_visibility lists the target among the visible rows (and makes its turn current) once the jump has landed. A jump to an id that is not in a populated transcript does nothing; in an empty transcript it is queued until rows mount and replaces the opening position.

use_message_scroller_scrollable() is a signal of which edges still have content (Scrollable { start, end }), fed by a message only when the value changes, never per scroll event or per token. While you are following the stream, end stays false, so a "new messages" affordance does not flicker on every chunk.

use_message_scroller_visibility() is a signal of Visibility { current_anchor_id, visible_message_ids }, for a table of contents, an "active turn" highlight or a "you are here" outline:

let visibility = use_message_scroller_visibility();
let current = visibility().current_anchor_id; // Option<String>: the turn being read
  • current_anchor_id is the message_id of the last scroll_anchor row whose top has reached the reading line: the top of the viewport plus scroll_margin plus scroll_previous_item_peek. It stays set after that turn scrolls off the top, so a table of contents does not flicker between turns; it is None before the first anchor is reached.
  • visible_message_ids lists, in document order, the rows with a message_id that are at least partly inside the viewport and below the reading line. A row hidden under the previous-turn peek is not listed, which matches what the reader can read.
  • It costs nothing until used. The controller starts an IntersectionObserver only when the first component calls the hook and stops it when the last one unmounts, and it reports only when the value changes, never per scroll event or per streamed token. A transcript that never calls the hook runs no observer.
  • The visibility example shows a header that follows the turn being read.

Entrances are plain CSS, not a scroller feature: put an entrance class on the row's own element (the Message inside the MessageScrollerItem) and it plays once when the row mounts. dx-effects.css ships three, ported from shadcn's presets, next to the theme's dx-fade-in, dx-pop-in and dx-drop-in:

  • dx-enter-spring-bounce: rises 12px and settles from a 0.96 scale with a spring overshoot (a CSS linear() easing; no script).
  • dx-enter-blur-fade: fades in from a 4px blur while rising 6px.
  • dx-enter-slide-side: slides in 18px from the inline-end edge (flipped in RTL; the distance is --dx-enter-slide-x).

They animate only opacity, scale, translate and filter (never transform, and never height, margin or padding), so the row's measured height is identical on every frame and turn anchoring keeps working while it plays. They play only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; with reduced motion the row appears at once. Store the preset with the row when it is sent (as the animation example does) so changing it later does not replay rows already on screen. slide-up and scale-fade are not shipped: the theme's dx-drop-in and dx-fade-in cover them.

The root and viewport carry these attributes, written by the controller rather than by Rust, so a later render never overwrites them:

  • data-scrollable: "start", "end", "start end", or absent.
  • data-autoscrolling: present while a programmatic scroll to the end runs.
  • data-pending-scroll: present until the opening position is applied.

The button carries data-active ("true" when there is content in its direction) and is inert otherwise.

MessageScrollerViewport takes fade: ScrollFade, which puts the matching dx-scroll-fade-* class on the viewport, the element that actually scrolls (never the root frame). The default is ScrollFade::Bottom, Nova's end-edge hint; ScrollFade::Top suits a thread that opens at its newest messages and loads history upward, ScrollFade::Y fades both edges and ScrollFade::None adds nothing.

MessageScrollerViewport { fade: ScrollFade::Top,
    MessageScrollerContent { .. }
}
  • The fade is a CSS scroll-driven mask on the viewport (see the dx-scroll-fade utility in the ScrollArea docs), so it follows the viewport's scroll offset: it is unaffected by content-visibility rows and by prepended history, and a transcript that fits has no fade. A browser without scroll-driven animations gets a static edge fade.
  • It needs dx-effects.css linked once at the app root next to the theme; message_scroller's component.json lists it in globalAssets, so shadcn-dioxus add message_scroller copies it. It cannot live in this component's style.css: the file also holds the @property registrations and keyframes every scroller shares, and a second copy would be a second set of declarations to keep in step.
  • The mask also dissolves the viewport's own border and background, so keep those on a wrapper (the demos do) and let the viewport be the inner element.
  • Examples: the fade variant (history above fades; the buttons switch edge and prepend earlier messages).

  • Rows are always real elements (see Virtualization), so the accessibility tree sees the whole transcript, and find-in-page does too in browsers that search skipped content.
  • The styled viewport has a bottom edge fade from dx-effects.css (the fade prop's default, ScrollFade::Bottom). Without that file the fade is simply absent. See Edge fade below.
  • On a renderer without document::eval (native/Blitz) the shell renders as plain overflow: no auto-follow, no flash guard, and an inert button.

The jump button slides, scales and fades with --dx-motion-duration-slow when it shows and a literal 0.4s when it hides; the transcript is revealed once its scroll position has been applied (the flash guard). Reduced motion swaps in --dx-motion-duration-reduced. Nothing loops, so nothing is paused while the scroller is unseen. See Motion for the tokens, reduced motion and the per-component table.

Not reproduced: the slide-up and scale-fade animation presets as separate classes (the theme's dx-drop-in and dx-fade-in are the same motion), and a boolean return from the scroll commands (they are fire-and-forget by design; see Commands). A composer whose actions sit in a full-width bottom row is InputGroupAlign::BlockEnd (see the Input Group docs).

auto_scrollboolfalse

Follow new content while the reader is at the live edge. Scrolling away (wheel, touch, scroll keys, scrollbar drag, an explicit jump) releases it; the jump button or MessageScrollerApi::scroll_to_end re-engages it. Off by default: nothing moves unless asked to.

default_scroll_positionDefaultScrollPositionDefault::default()

Where a saved transcript opens, applied once on the first non-empty render. The value at mount also decides whether the flash guard renders; a later change re-applies the new opening position (without hiding the viewport again).

scroll_edge_thresholdf648.0

Distance in pixels from an edge that still counts as "at" that edge.

scroll_previous_item_peekf6464.0

Pixels of the previous row kept visible above a newly anchored row.

scroll_marginf640.0

Extra margin in pixels on the aligned edge for anchoring and jumps.

virtualizeVirtualizationDefault::default()

How off-screen rows are kept cheap. Defaults to Virtualization::ContentVisibility.

childrenElementempty

The scroller's parts.

MessageScrollerProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScroller component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
childrenElementempty

The viewport and any controls.

Plus the global attributes.

MessageScrollerViewportProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScrollerViewport component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
preserve_scroll_on_prependbooltrue

Keep the first visible row where it is when older rows are prepended. On by default.

fadeScrollFadeScrollFade::Bottom

A scroll-edge fade on the viewport, which is the element that scrolls (the dx-scroll-fade-* classes of dx-effects.css; see ScrollFade). Defaults to ScrollFade::Bottom, the Nova transcript's end-edge hint; pass ScrollFade::Top for a thread that opens at the bottom and loads history upward, ScrollFade::Y for both edges or ScrollFade::None for none. The fade follows the scroll offset of the viewport, so it is unaffected by content-visibility rows and by prepended history.

childrenElementempty

The MessageScrollerContent.

Plus the global attributes.

MessageScrollerContentProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScrollerContent component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
spacer_classStringNone

A class for the internal tail spacer used when anchoring a turn near the top.

childrenElementempty

The rows: every direct child should be a MessageScrollerItem.

Plus the global attributes.

MessageScrollerItemProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScrollerItem component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
message_idStringNone

A stable row id, for MessageScrollerApi::scroll_to_message and prepend preservation. Rows without one still scroll and anchor but cannot be jumped to or preserved.

scroll_anchorboolfalse

Marks a turn boundary: a newly appended anchor is scrolled near the top, and DefaultScrollPosition::LastAnchor opens on the last one.

childrenElementempty

The row's content: a message, marker, typing indicator, separator or "load earlier" row.

Plus the global attributes.

MessageScrollerRowsProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScrollerRows component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
countusizerequired

How many rows there are.

startisize0

The absolute position of row 0 (default 0). Rows are grouped by absolute position, so when older rows are prepended, lower start by the number prepended: every existing row then stays in its chunk and keeps its DOM node. (Appending needs no change.)

render_rowCallback<usize, Element>required

Renders row index (an index into 0..count): a MessageScrollerItem.

Plus the global attributes.

MessageScrollerButtonProps Primitive

The props for the MessageScrollerButton component.

PropTypeDefaultDescription
directionMessageScrollerDirectionDefault::default()

The transcript edge to scroll toward.

behaviorScrollBehaviorScrollBehavior::Smooth

How the viewport moves. Smooth by default.

onclickEventHandler<MouseEvent>None

Called before the scroll; call prevent_default() to cancel it.

asCallback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>None

Render a different element instead of the default button, keeping the scroll behaviour and the controller-owned state attributes.

childrenElementempty

The button's content (an icon plus a screen-reader label).

Plus the <button> element's attributes.

Examples

Alternative examples for common configurations.

last anchor

Hi! I am wiring up a saved conversation.
Great, what should it do when someone reopens it?
Where should it open: the very bottom, or somewhere better?
Somewhere better. Reopening at the absolute end drops you into the middle of an answer.
So where do I land?
On your last message, with its reply below it. You see what you asked and where the answer starts, and you can read down from there without reconstructing the thread from the bottom edge. If the last turn is short enough to fit in the viewport the scroller falls back to the end, so you never see a blank gap under it.
And this last one is the message it opens on.
That is the `LastAnchor` position. It is keyed on the rows marked with `scroll_anchor`, not on a role, so a system marker or a handoff event can be the anchor just as well. The viewport stays hidden until the position is applied, which is what keeps a server-rendered page from flashing the top of the thread first. This reply is intentionally long: a turn that does not fit in the viewport is the case where opening at the last message differs from opening at the end. Scroll down to read the rest, or press the button to jump to the end. A saved thread is a place you are returning to, so the first thing on screen should be a place to start reading from, not the last line of whatever was said last. Opening at the end is still available: it is the default, and the right choice when the newest message is what you came back for.

A saved thread opens at its last anchor.

2000 messages in the DOM

A 2,000-row transcript through MessageScrollerRows.

commands

Commands
Drive the transcript from outside.

We're seeing activation dip after workspace creation. Can you help me find the likely step?

The sharpest drop is between creating the workspace and inviting the first teammate.

Workspace creation is still healthy, but the invite step is where users pause. That suggests the product is asking for collaboration before the user has enough confidence in the workspace.

What should I compare before we change the onboarding flow?

Compare three cohorts:

1. Users who choose a template before inviting teammates. 2. Users who start from a blank workspace. 3. Users who skip invites and return within 24 hours.

If template users invite faster, the fix is probably better first-run guidance rather than a louder invite prompt.

Can you turn that into an experiment?

Yes. Create a variant that shows a short checklist after workspace creation:

- Pick a template. - Add one project detail. - Invite a teammate when the workspace has context.

Measure first invite completion, 24-hour return rate, and whether teams create a second project.

What's the risk if we delay the invite prompt?

The main risk is reducing team creation for accounts that already know who they want to invite.

To protect that path, keep the invite action visible in the header and only change the primary empty-state guidance. That gives confident teams a direct route without forcing uncertain users through the invite step too early.

Use the controls to jump to any message in the conversation.

A "Jump to..." menu calls use_message_scroller().scroll_to_message(id, ScrollToMessageOptions { align: ScrollAlign::Start, behavior: ScrollBehavior::Smooth }) for each user turn. The menu lives inside the provider, so it reaches the same controller as the transcript.

Toggle the anchor role, then send messages to compare where turns settle.

scroll_anchor is a per-row prop, not a role. A toggle picks whether user or assistant rows are the anchors; choosing the other role resets the thread, so you can compare where the turns settle.

Workspace creation rose 8%, but first invite completion only rose 2%.

Start with the invite step. Teams are creating workspaces but waiting to add collaborators.

Recommended follow-up:

1. Compare invite drop-off by account size. 2. Check whether users who skip invites still return within 24 hours. 3. Review the empty-state copy on the first project screen. 4. Segment activation by template, since template users may not need invites right away.

If that pattern holds, the next experiment should make collaboration useful earlier instead of prompting for invites harder.

Toggle the default_scroll_position to see where the transcript starts when you open the thread.

Tabs for Start, End and LastAnchor. default_scroll_position is live: a new choice changes the provider's prop and the mounted transcript re-applies the opening position (the flash guard only covers the first paint, so the viewport is not hidden again).

previous context

Keeping Context Visible
New turns keep part of the previous reply in view.

I'm building a chat for our app and the scroll behavior is driving me nuts. Every time the AI streams a reply, the whole thread jumps around.

That's the classic streaming scroll problem. Wrap your message list in `MessageScroller` and turn on `autoScroll` -- the viewport pins to the bottom as tokens arrive, so users always see the latest text land in place.

The important part: it only auto-scrolls while the reader is already at the bottom. The moment they scroll up to read something earlier, auto-scroll backs off and their position is preserved. You get smooth streaming without fighting the user's intent.

64px

Adjust the slider and send. Observe the previous message peek.

A slider drives scroll_previous_item_peek (64 to 128 px), together with scroll_margin. Send the next queued message to see how much of the previous reply stays visible above the new turn.

This will create a marker and make it the anchor

When a user joins, a marker is created. scroll_anchor on the marker marks it as the next turn.

A join Marker with variant: MarkerVariant::Separator is a MessageScrollerItem with scroll_anchor, so an event row can start a turn just as a user message does.

animation

Animation
Choose how user messages are animated when they are added to the conversation.
No Messages Yet
Click the button below to send the first message.

Select an animation then click send to see it in action.

User rows enter with one of six entrance keyframes, chosen in a Select: the theme's shared dx-fade-in, dx-pop-in and dx-drop-in, and dx-effects.css's dx-enter-spring-bounce (a linear() spring easing), dx-enter-blur-fade and dx-enter-slide-side. The preset in force when a row is sent is stored with that row, so changing it later never replays the rows already on screen. The keyframes animate only opacity, scale, translate and filter, so a row's measured height never changes while it plays and anchoring is unaffected; reduced motion shows the row at once.

visibility

Visibility
No turn yet, 0 rows in view

How do I read where the reader is in a long thread?

Subscribe to the scroller's visibility. It reports the current turn and the rows in view, and it only reports when they change.

Nothing is observed until the first subscriber mounts, so a transcript that never asks pays nothing.

What counts as the current turn?

The last user message whose top has reached the reading line: the top of the viewport plus the scroll margin plus the previous-item peek.

It stays current after it scrolls off the top, until the next turn arrives, so a table of contents does not flicker between turns.

And the visible rows?

Every row with a message id that is at least partly inside the viewport and below the reading line, in document order.

A row hidden under the peek of the previous turn is not listed, which matches what the reader can actually read.

Can I build a jump menu from it?

Yes: highlight the current turn in a list of user messages and call scroll_to_message from each entry.

Because the state is a signal, any component under the provider can read it.

Scroll the conversation; the header follows the turn you are reading.

use_message_scroller_visibility() returns the reader's position as a signal: current_anchor_id (the last turn anchor, here each user message, whose top has reached the reading line) and visible_message_ids (the rows in view, in document order). The header reads it to show which turn is current and how many rows are in view. The controller observes rows only while a subscriber is mounted, and reports only when the state changes, never per scroll event. The footer's two buttons call scroll_to_message with ScrollBehavior::Instant, one with the provider's margin and one with scroll_margin: Some(24.0) for that call only.
